name: sequence_recommender
intended_use: Suggest the next assistance action a helper is likely to need, ranked, and intersected with the admissible set.
out_of_scope_use: Suggestions are never executed automatically and never widen what the policy engine permits.
training_data: 793 synthetic assistance sessions with per-user behavioural bias.
model_type: first-order Markov chain with Jelinek-Mercer backoff
selection_criterion: Recall@3 and MRR on a chronological session split with held-out cold-start users; simplicity preferred at equal performance
limitations: First-order: conditions only on the immediately previous action, so a longer-range dependency is invisible to it.
Suggestions reflect what helpers have done before, which will reinforce existing habits including poor ones.
Synthetic sequences follow a hand-specified workflow; real sessions will be messier.
ethical_considerations: Suggesting remote control makes it more likely to be requested, so suggestions are filtered through the safety envelope before display.
Per-user models are built from that user's own history only and are never shared between accounts.
